## @oh-my-pi/pi-ai

### Fixed

- Cursor exec frames keep tool-batch order: a file mutation (native StrReplace and Write, `write`, `delete`, `pi_edit`, `pi_write`) waits for the calls issued before it, and the calls issued after it wait until it lands, so a Shell sent in the same batch as a StrReplace no longer runs before the edit's write ([#18434](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/18434) by [@KadirBerkpolat1](https://github.com/KadirBerkpolat1))
- ChatGPT Pro Max (`promax`) counts as Pro for Codex account routing, so a blocked Pro account no longer wins over an open or pinned Pro Max account ([#18399](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/18399) by [@serverinspector](https://github.com/serverinspector))
- Cursor Shell results no longer end with `Timeout clamped to 3600s (requested 86400s; …)`: Cursor's 24 h `hard_timeout` is capped at the bash tool's 3600 s ceiling before it reaches the tool ([#18433](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/18433) by [@KadirBerkpolat1](https://github.com/KadirBerkpolat1))
- A 429 or 402 worded like a context overflow (Bedrock's "429 Too many tokens, please wait…") is treated as a rate limit, so it retries and walks the fallback chain instead of compacting ([#18345](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/18345) by [@nick-maderight](https://github.com/nick-maderight))
- `auth-gateway stdio` and `serve` no longer reject credentialless Apple on-device models ([#18370](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/18370))

- The extension now requests `scripting` and access to all sites (Chrome lists "Read and change all your data on all websites"); it uses them only to empty another extension's frames in a tab omp is driving, when Chrome refuses it the debugger there ([#16908](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/pull/16908) by [@will-bogusz](https://github.com/will-bogusz))

## LDR 2.0

**LDR 2.0 is our biggest architectural change yet.** We rebuilt the web layer on FastAPI and Uvicorn, hardened security across the whole app, added new search engines, and made Stop actually stop research mid-generation. It took 1,010 commits in ten weeks, from 40 contributors, 31 of them new to the project. Thank you to everyone who built, tested and reported issues.

Several defaults and API contracts changed. **Read the upgrade notes before deploying**, especially if you run LDR behind a reverse proxy or call its HTTP API from your own clients.

### ⚠️ Before you upgrade

- **Take a verified offline backup first.** 2.0 changes your databases, and v1.10.7 can't use them afterwards. LDR's built-in backups aren't a substitute (see the next point). Never start v1.10.7 on upgraded data, because doing so can delete your remaining built-in backups. Follow the [upgrade and rollback guide](https://github.com/LearningCircuit/local-deep-research/blob/main/docs/deployment/upgrading.md), which also covers failed upgrades.
- **Pre-migration backups now live in their own folder.** Each user gets `encrypted_databases/backups/<user hash>/pre-migration/`. Copy that folder out of the data directory after each user's first sign-in. With the default retention (1 backup, 7 days), the first login backup after the upgrade removes the regular backups made before it. Raise **Max Backups** and **Backup Retention (days)** first if you want to keep them.
- **Check your settings and environment overrides.** Invalid configured values now raise an error instead of silently falling back to a default. This includes bad `LDR_*` booleans (only `true/1/yes/on/enabled` and `false/0/no/off/disabled` are accepted), `llm.request_timeout` below 1 second, and `llm.max_retries` outside 0–5. The settings page, research form and API errors name the offending key.

## Images are kept by default and show in My Work

- **Kept by default:** screenshots and images your agent reads or makes are now kept and linked to the observations from that turn, without sending them to an AI model. Image inference stays off (#5426).
- **"Keep images" switch:** the memory viewer's Settings has a new **Images** section. Turning **Keep images** off stops keeping new images; images already kept stay. A `"false"` you saved yourself is respected (#5426).
- **Gallery in My Work:** request cards show an image count and the first four thumbnails; the request drawer shows every linked image; any thumbnail opens a full-size gallery with keyboard navigation (#5427).
- **Fresh databases:** My Work lists observation activity again on a newly created database (#5427).
- **Local conversion you can rely on:** captured screenshots now convert on your own computer instead of failing as busy or timing out. Conversions wait their turn and get 20 seconds each, and every stored copy is lossy WebP so it stays small (#5431).
- **Cloud quota:** each owner can store up to 25 GiB of images on cmem.ai, the same limit Pro enforces (#5467).

## Fixes

- **Sessions:** after you delete a session in the viewer, new work in the same resumed conversation is captured again (#5463).
- **Sessions:** committed transcript entries are no longer replayed after a worker restart (#5321, thanks @lamimiahmed45-droid).
- **Hooks:** Grok Build's camelCase hook payload is accepted (#4282, thanks @nathan-v).
- **Hooks:** PreToolUse memory lookups are scoped to the current platform, so one harness no longer gets another's observations (#5008, thanks @SuperMarioYL).
- **My Work:** the scheduled refresh stays on the configured agent instead of falling back to another one (#5245, thanks @Dev-0710).
- **Claude CLI:** the Claude CLI is found again when `CLAUDE_CODE_PATH` changes (#5460, thanks @WhitePepperLambSoup).

_Automated prerelease from `develop` — **Server** v3.6.0._


### Added
- **server**: a seeded app version records the sha256 of the bundle it was copied from (`metadata.build.bundleSha256`), and `bundle_changed()` tells an orchestrator whether the pod's build differs from the app's newest seed, so a deploy can re-seed only the apps whose build changed. An app whose public version is a direct deploy, not a seed, counts as unchanged, so a release never replaces it
- **tool_github**: four reads for apps that work on repositories with credentials held in the node configuration: `repo_contributors`, `repo_languages`, `label_list` and `user_get` (the PAT user, or the App itself under App auth). They return `{status, data, rate_limit, next_page}`: rate-limit counters from the response headers, the next page number from the `Link` header, and a non-2xx answer as a result with `status`, `message` and `documentation_url` rather than an exception; tokens, private keys and bearer headers never appear in a result or an error message. Existing tools keep their return shapes (#2592)
- **tool_github**: `repo_tree` lists a repository recursively at a branch, tag or SHA (default `HEAD`, the default branch), sorted by path, with GitHub's `truncated` flag and a `complete` flag of its own, in the result envelope of the repository reads. With `walk: true` a listing GitHub truncated is completed from subtree reads pinned to the SHA the ref resolved to, so a branch that moves during the walk cannot mix revisions: each subtree is read recursively and only one GitHub truncates again is split into its direct children, so a repository the size of Linux takes tens of requests. `max_requests` (default 1000) and `max_entries` (default 200000) bound the walk; the entry cap is what stops a git bomb, where a few trees referenced from thousands of paths multiply entries while requests stay few. ```bash
OLD_VERSION=0.7.10  # replace with the Core version your project uses today
npm install @astryxdesign/core@0.7.11 @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.11  # plus every other @astryxdesign/* package you use, at 0.7.11

## @astryxdesign/core

### New Features

- Under a finger (a coarse primary pointer, on any touch device), Popover grows out of its trigger, wide before tall, with its edge held on the trigger, and shrinks back into the trigger when it closes. The growth plays the theme's `--duration-medium-min` (in the Storybook theme, the step nearest iOS's 206 ms growth) with its entrance easing, and the shrink plays its exit duration and easing, on the compositor. A close during the growth, or an open during the shrink, turns back from where the popover is. With reduced motion it cross-fades in and out, opacity only, in 200 ms or less. A fine primary pointer (a mouse) keeps its entrance. A tap that lands while it grows is ignored, and a pan started then scrolls nothing. The shrink plays on the layer runtime's exit copy, of which Popover is the first user. The growth starts in the next animation frame, before that frame paints, so the opening tap does no extra layout. (#8187)
- `DropdownMenuSubMenu` accepts `delay` and `hideDelay`, in milliseconds, the same options `Tooltip`, `HoverCard` and `TopNavMenu` have. `delay` is how long a hovering pointer waits before the flyout opens (default 150), and `hideDelay` is how long the flyout stays after the pointer leaves (default 200). The defaults match today's timing, so nothing changes unless you pass them. Keyboard focus and touch never wait. (#10298)

What a 44-site test of 2.5.0 showed, fixed: builds now iterate until the checker is clean, every page moves, products without photographs are shown in photographs, palettes fit the trade, the copy gets a voice of its own, and nothing lies on anything else on a phone. The install name did not change.

- **A finish gate:** `scripts/gate.mjs` runs the checker, the layout check and a copy lint, and a build is not done until its last line reads `GATE: PASS` (three rounds, five waivers with reasons at most). In Claude Code it runs as a Stop hook from the skill itself. It never traps an agent: a question to the user costs no round, and `gate.mjs --done` ends a build at the user's word.
- **Motion on every page:** every hero enters once on load, and every page carries one or two scroll moments. Cafes, shops and services get photo- and type-led ones (new `photo-chapters`, a film look for `picture-develops`); shader effects stay on tech pages.
- **Photographs over renders:** a product without the client's pictures is shown in licensed stand-in photographs (`photos.mjs search`: Wikimedia Commons, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA and public domain only). A 3D render only when the brief asks for one.
- **Palettes by trade:** `start.mjs deal --trade cafe` deals palettes made for that trade, so two cafes no longer start alike. Eight new place palettes.
- **A copy layer:** a fact sheet, a voice card, one register and the moves for each part of the page, plus `copy-lint.mjs`, which counts the tells of model-written copy. The gate runs it.
- **Accessibility, forms and metadata:** accessible names, labels, the focus ring, heading order, share tags and real form sends are checked.
- **Phones:** sections grow with their content instead of lying over the next one, 44px tap targets, a phone action bar that waits until the hero's button has scrolled away, and new `collide`, `tap-size` and 320px checks.
- **A kit that passes its own checks:** all 11 hero layouts, the starter and two in-page moment mode

body:
## Pro sign-in works again

Signing in to cmem.ai Pro from the plugin returned a 500 error on every fresh plugin install. The plugin's install did not include `better-auth`, and its tables were never created. The plugin now ships `better-auth` and `@better-auth/api-key` as dependencies and creates the auth tables the first time they are needed (#5455, thanks @0xABCD01).

## Fixes

- **Worker:** when a run pauses after a transport, rate-limit or similar abort, it now releases its claims, so the paused session no longer holds pending work that can never expire (#5457, thanks @akashpandey).
- **Worker:** an over-budget condense reply is clamped to the budget instead of being thrown away (#5452, thanks @xunguangzlj-cloud).
- **Worker:** retry-without-reasoning now recognizes OpenCode Go's "cannot be represented" error wording (#5439, thanks @akashpandey).
- **Hooks:** the Stop hook reads Claude Code's `last_assistant_message` directly and skips reading the transcript (#5449, thanks @xunguangzlj-cloud).
- **Context:** the OAuth hint and gateway fallback notice are reserved before the context is fitted, so SessionStart context stays under Claude Code's 10,000-character limit (#5441, thanks @liuyinchu).
- **Codex:** stale app-server child processes are recycled on the auth recovery probe (#5438, thanks @akashpandey).
- **Installer:** the Goose YAML config is written atomically, so an interrupted install or uninstall can no longer leave a truncated config.yaml (#5442, thanks @DeryFerd).
- **Tests:** the sync matrix waits for the page body before reading it, fixing a browser readiness race (#5448).

## Also in this release

- **My Work:** the scheduled refresh check interval is now a setting (#5437, thanks @weirui828).
- **Docs:** one story across the README and docs: your coding agent forgets between sessions, Claude-Mem remembers (#5447).
- **Docs:** README translations keep fenced code examples and single-quoted links intact (#5458, thanks @Afloat16).

Univer 1.4.0 adds Office attachment workflows, shape merging in Slides, richer pivot filtering, and `GETPIVOTDATA`. This release also separates product-specific comment integrations and introduces several package and API migrations.

## New features

### Office attachments across Sheets, Docs, and Slides

Preserve embedded OLE files when working with Office documents, with actions to preview, download, rename, and delete attachments. Supported Office files can also be converted into independent online documents when the application provides the required collaboration, attachment, and exchange services.

Office export keeps the original embedded file by default. Applications can request the current confirmed version of a converted online document instead:

```ts
import { ExchangeFormat } from '@univerjs-pro/exchange-client';

const file = await univerAPI.exportSheetByUnitIdAsync(
    unitId,
    ExchangeFormat.XLSX,
    undefined,
    { oleAttachmentSource: 'online' }
);
```

The server must support this export option. Cross-type Office previews require the corresponding existing product UI module; conversion and preview use the existing drawing and exchange plugins.

### Merge shapes in Slides

Combine supported selections with **Union, Combine, Fragment, Intersect, and Subtract**. The operations create new shape geometry and support undo/redo and collaboration. The first selected object determines the primary formatting and the subtraction direction.

### Multiple filters and whole-day date filtering

Pivot tables and pivot charts can combine different filter categories on the same field after enabling **Allow multiple filters per field**. The option is off by default.

Fixed date filters also support **whole-day comparison**, so timestamps from the same day can match without requiring identical time values.

## Fork chats from any reply, Plan mode & a faster phone ✨

- 📱 **A smoother experience on your phone:** The phone opens and reconnects sooner, scrolls and streams chats more smoothly, reads Markdown and math better, and keeps unsent chat, review and Tasks text across reconnects.
- 🗂️ **Organize workspaces across machines:** Nest workspaces under a folder workspace, including workspaces on other machines.
- 🌿 **Do more with Chat UI:** Fork any finished response to try another direction while the original chat stays as it was. In Claude or Codex chats, type `/plan` to switch to Plan mode, which persists when you reopen the chat.
- 🖥️ **A more reliable terminal:** Terminal panes keep their zoom and restored scrollback, copied files paste as full paths, and busy terminal output takes less work to render.
- 🤖 **Better agent support:** Open running subagents from chat, see proposed files and diffs in Codex approvals, answer OpenCode choice questions, and sign in to Antigravity Chat with Gemini Enterprise.
- 🎙️ **Better dictation:** Pick your dictation language, keep the first and last words, see Listening while the model loads, and get on-device text back about a third sooner.
- 🧭 **Know where a chat runs:** The chat composer shows the machine, workspace and branch, and chats show a card for each pull request the agent opens.
- ⚡ **Snappier desktop chats:** One chat's status change no longer wakes every chat, the model picker opens without walking every worktree, and long replies stream without re-rendering.

# Paperclip v2026.1106.0

> Released: 2026-11-06

Paperclip v2026.1106.0 carries 515 commits, promoted from `2026.1023.0-beta.0`. The headline is that the Paperclip Runner is now the default for new agents: new Claude, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi agents start on the native Runner on qualified macOS and Linux hosts, existing agents get a one-click "Upgrade runner" action, and GitHub Copilot joins as a native harness. Around that: project repositories that automatically become skill sources, model-backed prompt injection prevention, agent observability to Braintrust or any OTLP endpoint, a unified Google Workspace connection, bulk edits on the Agents roster, workspaces that compact and expire themselves with encrypted restore points, and Grok Bot and Muse as experimental Runner providers. Underneath, server restarts report ready sooner, the Docker image boots from a precompiled bundle, task pages load faster, and more background services stop polling the database.

## Breaking Changes

- **The Pipelines experiment is removed.** Pipeline boards, stage settings, case automation, review queues, the `pipelines` CLI commands, the `pipelines:write` permission, the `enablePipelines` setting, and the `linkedCases` field on task detail are gone; Cases and Routines remain. Existing pipeline tables and records are preserved untouched and a stored `enablePipelines` value is ignored. ([#16834](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16834))
- **Run failures no longer reach Sentry by default.** A backend DSN alone no longer reports agent run failures. Set `PAPERCLIP_SENTRY_RUN_FAILURES=unexpected` to keep the previous filtered policy or `all` to report every failed or timed-out run; the default is `off`. ([#16300](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/16300))
- **The run history list is bounded.** `GET /api/companies/{companyId}/heartbeat-runs` returns 200 rows by default and at most 1,000; clients that relied on an unbounded array must pass an explicit `limit`. ([#16286]

# Installer screen telemetry and runtime fixes

Claude-Mem now records progress through the local setup screens, so the admin can show where setup continues, goes back, encounters a known error, or has no recorded next step.

- Track the nine actual setup screens: Scan, Reveal, Choose memory, Review savings, Checkout, Finish setup, Import history, Launch, and Workspace.
- Count each rendered screen visit separately. Returning to a screen creates a new visit; failed hand-offs do not become successful forward transitions.
- Preserve the real setup branches. At Home and existing Pro configurations skip checkout, history import returns to Finish setup, and reduced-motion setup skips the launch animation.
- Record local setup completion only after the worker accepts the successful setup state write.
- Preserve pending screen events when setup finishes and retry temporary local-worker connection failures, so a fast completion or a slow telemetry request does not lose the visit history.
- Pass a fresh setup-attempt ID through the existing installer pairing when telemetry is enabled, allowing the matching admin report to connect setup progress to the authorized account flow.

The events follow the existing analytics settings, including `DO_NOT_TRACK`. Their schema accepts only known screen IDs, actions, error codes, timestamps, and random attempt/visit IDs. Prompts, filenames, URLs, credentials, and free-form error text are excluded. Sample previews do not emit setup events. The worker's long-lived anonymous identity is not aliased to an account.

Per-screen history starts with this release. Older installers did not record these screens, so their missing events are not treated as zero conversions or abandonment.

## What's changed

- Changed auto mode with telemetry or feature flags off, including behind LLM gateways: calls the server can't check are asked about or denied, with no fallback to the built-in classifier; set `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0` to keep using it (Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry are unchanged)
- Changed auto mode behind an LLM gateway: `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=1` turns on the server-side check even with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS` set; if managed settings set the latter, they must set the `1` too
- Added support for MCP tasks in the terminal: when an MCP server runs a tool call as a task, Claude Code moves it to the background right away and tells Claude the result when it finishes
- Added the `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND` environment variable to make Claude Code wait for an MCP task inside its tool call instead of moving it to the background right away
- Added `permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting` setting: a tool call that would wait on a permission prompt is denied and the turn continues, in terminal sessions, subagents and teammates
- Added `/claude-api latency-optimize` to find where your Claude API code makes people wait and try faster settings against your eval
- Added the `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEATURE_FLAGS` environment variable, which stops feature-flag fetching without turning off telemetry; every flag then uses its built-in default
- Added spend for today, this week and this month to `/usage` for developers behind a Claude apps gateway who have no spend limit, when the gateway runs this version or later
- Added `admin.pooled_conflict_rule` and `admin.pooled_priority_order` to the Claude apps gateway, to set which pooled group budget pays first for a developer in several groups
- Added an optional `login_notice` setting to the Claude apps gateway that shows an operator-defined message on the gateway's browser verification page and on Claude Code's sign-in screen

ui/pose-fusion/pkg/ruvector-attention is a wasm-pack build of
ruvector-attention-wasm vendored for the browser demo; the npm package is
published from ruvnet/ruvector. The vendored manifest declared the same
name without "private", so RuView looked like a second publisher of that

npm-published from this repo. Runtime is unchanged: the demo loads the
files by relative path.

* fix(harness): bound @ruvnet/ruview-kernel peer range to ^0.1.0

">=0.1.0" accepted any future major of the optional kernel peer
(release:open_range). ^0.1.0 matches the 0.x line the bridge was written
against; the ruview umbrella already pins kernel 0.1.0 exactly.

Co-Authored-By: claude-flow <ruv@ruv.net>

* fix(mobile): refresh lockfile for npm audit advisories, raise axios floor

npm audit fix (no --force) on ui/mobile: critical 1 -> 0, high 20 -> 4
(prod tree: critical 1 -> 0, high 18 -> 4). Fixed include shell-quote
(critical), axios, @react-navigation/core, ws, node-forge, form-data,

## Security dependency fix

- **`@ruvector/attention` 2.2.3.**
  - `claude-flow` 3.72.1 declared `@ruvector/attention ^0.1.3`, and `ruvector` 0.3.12 also depended on `^0.1.3`. Both resolved to 0.1.32, which lacks the upstream fix (RuVector #1365): input-length validation, and catching Rust panics at the NAPI boundary so they don't abort Node.
  - 3.72.2 moves to `ruvector ^0.3.13`, which depends on `attention ^2.2.3`, in the CLI, `claude-flow` and `ruflo`. `claude-flow` also declares `attention ^2.2.3` directly.
  - Every attention call ruflo makes (Flash, MoE, Hyperbolic, AdamW, InfoNCE, Curriculum, `compute`) was checked on 0.1.32 and 2.2.3. The results match.
- **`@ruvector/sona` 0.1.11.** `@claude-flow/neural` 3.0.3 (published standalone) pins `@ruvector/sona` 0.1.11, up from 0.1.5. On 0.1.5:
  - a wrong-length input to `applyMicroLora` panicked in Rust and aborted Node (exit 134);
  - `findPatterns` returned 0 patterns after training.

  On 0.1.11 the bad input throws a catchable error, and learning returns patterns.

## Fixes

- **`neural benchmark`: the attention benchmark now runs.** It never had:
  - `import()` of the CommonJS package put its classes on `default`;
  - it called `computeRaw()`, which no release has, instead of `compute()`.
- **Plugins (#4842), shipped through the marketplace:**
  - `ruflo-ruvector` 0.4.0, `ruflo-browser` 0.3.8, `ruflo-console` 0.49.12 and `ruflo-agentdb` 0.4.12 move to ruvector 0.3.12.
  - The browser recording recipes used `trajectory-*` flags that no ruvector release accepts. They are fixed.
  - The CLI's browser-session npx fallback pins `ruvector@0.3.12`.

- **`claude-flow` now lists `@ruvector/attention` as a regular dependency.** On npm 10 / Node 20, `@ruvector/ruvllm-gpu-loop` (requires node >=22) fails as an optional install, and npm then drops ruvllm, ruvector and every package reached only through optional edges. The patched attention is now always installed.

A bug-fix release. No new settings and no breaking changes.

## Reliability

- Context reads keep working when the database's `-wal` and wal-index files are missing. (#5432 by @0xABCD01)
- Queued batches are kept, not dropped, when Claude replies with a 429 rate limit. (#5430 by @markjoin123)
- A stalled session's buffered work is discarded once its resume attempts are used up, so it no longer blocks the queue. (#5414 by @0xABCD01)
- SSE frames queued for a slow consumer are now bounded. (#5395 by @liuyinchu)
- The observer response deadline has its own constant. (#5406 by @lunetics)
- The observer fills missing proxy settings from your Claude user settings. (#5401 by @markjoin123)
- `/api/processing-status` reports sessions the stall pacer abandoned and the observer's last successful store time. (#5409, #5408 by @xunguangzlj-cloud)
- Settings: SessionStart toggles persist, and zero context counts are accepted via `POST /api/settings`. (#5393 by @0xABCD01)

## Security

- All TeamBrain routes reject requests from foreign origins. (#5411 by @DeryFerd)
- Perplexity API keys are redacted. (#5407 by @mertkayacs)

## Viewer and My Work

- My Work sharing stays on for the cloud viewer. (#5433 by @thedotmack)
- Unparseable work-view frames are dropped instead of throwing. (#5412 by @DeryFerd)
- Hosted usage reaches PostHog again (`randomUUID` is called on `crypto`). (#5421 by @thedotmack)
- Windows file paths are shortened on observation cards. (#5419 by @Plastic-time)

## Search and smart-read

- Dumb search keeps fetchable memories ahead of prompts. (#5397 by @liuyinchu)
- Search recalls supplementary Han and extended Katakana characters. (#5396 by @liuyinchu)
- Outlines include C and C++ unions, and Zig struct, enum, union and opaque declarations. (#5403, #5402 by @L4XB)

## Install, CLI and platforms

> **Repairs and docs; no new skill or mode, and the prompt-level changes are unmeasured:** An `experiment_provenance[]` entry can now say it has no honest lock values, with `repro_lock: null` and a `repro_lock_reason` (#1049). A survey or an analysis with no LLM could pass before only with placeholder values. Earlier ARS releases reject this form, so a passport that uses it needs this release. `check_repro_lock.py` now fails a required value that breaks its field's type or value rule, such as a null model id; `cross_model.secondary_model_id` may still be null. `planned_vs_executed[].value` accepts only a number or a string, so some passports that passed before now fail (#1050). The `sr-screener` methods text no longer says the reviewers could read only the record file: the tool list removes web and write access, and reading only the given file is an instruction (#1039). SETUP records two checks in which an uploaded skill dispatched a built-in sub-agent in a conversation after a retry; multi-agent stages stay untested (#1040).

### Fixed

- **An experiment with no honest lock values can say so (#1049, PR #1051).** Every `experiment_provenance[]` entry had to fill every `repro_lock` field, and those fields describe LLM and ARS run settings. A survey, an analysis with no LLM, or a trained model with no ARS prompts could pass only with placeholder values. The key stays required. Its value may now be `null`, and `repro_lock_reason` is then required; a reason beside a populated lock is rejected. The reason is free text: it discloses the gap, does not prove the lock does not apply, and no script checks the details it names. The passport-level validator and the required-field set do not change. **Compatibility:** earlier ARS releases reject `repro_lock: null` in an entry, so a passport that uses it needs this release.
- **`repro_lock` docs, example, gate, and validators agree (#1050, PR #1052).** `check_repro_lock.py` now checks each required value against its field's type

#### New Features

- `astryx discover` lists the experimental CircleCheckIndicator component from `@astryxdesign/lab`.
- `astryx theme build` keeps a theme's `componentIcons` slot functions. The built module imports each slot function from the module the theme source imports it from, writes static slot values beside it as JSON, and reads back the same static `componentIcons` view, so component icon slots resolve the same for the built theme as for the runtime theme. This includes slots inherited from a built, package, or family base. A slot function defined in the theme file still fails the build: move it to its own module and import it. In `--family` output, a member supplies its own slot functions through a named import of its whole `componentIcons` map. The module keeps each slot import as the theme source spells it (`--icons-specifier` rewrites only the icon registry import), so with `--out` in another directory, a module must answer to that specifier from the output directory.
- A theme chooses which shared icon a component's own icon role uses, by slot, with `defineTheme({componentIcons})`. The first slot is `code-block-copy`: CodeBlock's copy button passes `{copied}` and, with no theme entry, draws `copy`, then `check` while copied. A slot value is a shared icon name, `null` to hide the icon, a partial `{icon, variant, size}` request, or a pure function of the slot's state that returns one; a field the request leaves out keeps the component's own value. ## Fixed

- **Native Windows: the draw.io CLI is found again.** The Windows installer names the executable `draw.io.exe` (with the dot), while the scripts used the bare name `drawio`. `drawio2pptx.py`, `drawiohtml.py`, `svgflow.py`, and `timelapse.py` crashed with `FileNotFoundError`; `buildup.py` and `prdiff.py` reported the CLI as missing and skipped images. All of them, plus `diagramctl.py doctor`, now share one `drawio_cli.resolve_drawio()` resolver. It tries `drawio` and `draw.io` on PATH, then the macOS app bundle and the Windows `%ProgramFiles%`, `%ProgramFiles(x86)%`, and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` install directories, and passes the **absolute path** to subprocess. That also rules out `.cmd` shims, which Windows `CreateProcess` cannot launch (#143).
- **`explain.py` on Windows**: redirected Markdown is written as UTF-8, so arrows and other non-ASCII text no longer fail under a legacy code page.

## Changed

- **SVG text labels**: documented the per-cell `convertToSvg=1;` style for web-destined diagrams, its conversion limits and version gate, and the re-export caveat; the SVG and HTML exporter docs link to it.
- **PPTX export**: documented that `drawio2pptx.py` embeds a raster image per slide rather than individually editable PowerPoint shapes.
- **Installation docs**: corrected the manual placement recipe and the update attribution; the website install tabs match.
- **Japanese README**: `README_JA.md` added, linked from the language row.

## Tests

- 255 tests pass, 4 skipped. Seven new tests cover the resolver: PATH priority, the dotted name, the macOS app-bundle fallback, both Windows install directories, the nothing-installed case, and PATH hits winning over install locations.
- The `--embed-svg-images` regression test now asserts that the resolved absolute path reaches argv, not a bare name.
- CI runs on Ubuntu without draw.io installed, so the resolver is also exercised on the negative path.

3.72.0 brings ruflo's MCP server up to the [MCP 2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog) revision ([ADR-524](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/main/v3/docs/adr/ADR-524-mcp-2026-07-28-dual-era-stdio.md), #4837). It also merges 39 contributor fixes and tests from the [#4775](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/issues/4775) tracker and the daily security scan through [#4825](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/pull/4825). Thanks to every contributor.

## MCP 2026-07-28
`ruflo mcp start` now serves 2026-07-28 clients and older ones from the same process.
- **No more pinned version.** `initialize` used to answer `2024-11-05` whatever the client asked for. It now echoes a supported version (`2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18` or `2024-11-05`) and reports the real ruflo version.
- **`server/discover`** is answered, so a 2026-07-28 client's stdio probe finds ruflo.
- **Stateless requests.** A request that carries its version in `_meta` gets `resultType` and `serverInfo` on the result. An unsupported version is refused with `-32022` and the list of versions ruflo supports.
- **Stable tool list.** `tools/list` is sorted by name and carries cache hints, so the catalogue is identical on every call and client prompt caches keep hitting.
- **Tracing.** A W3C `traceparent` from the client is passed through to the tool call.

The Tasks extension and the HTTP server's move to 2026-07-28 are planned next (ADR-524, Phase 2).

## Security
- **pre-bash blocks a command it cannot check.** Before, late, unparsable or malformed hook input let the command through (#4743, #4826). The input window for pre-bash is now 3 s, so a slow host still gets its commands checked.
- **Browser tools** accept only http(s) and `about:blank` URLs. Screenshots are written inside the project. A project's Ollama `baseUrl` no longer receives your `OLLAMA_API_KEY` (#4812).
- **Statusline** runs sqlite3 without a shell and strips control characters from directory and git names (#4745, #481
name: v3.72.0 — MCP 2026-07-28 support + 39 contributor fixes

# Hermes Agent v0.23.0

**Release Date:** November 5, 2026
**Since v0.22.0:** ~10,080 commits · ~1,950 merged PRs · ~8,720 files changed · ~725,200 insertions · ~201,400 deletions · **~850 issues closed** · 666 contributors

> **The Hearth Release.** In the old hymns Hermes kept the threshold and Hestia kept the hearth, and the two were honored side by side. v0.22.0 got newcomers through the door; v0.23.0 builds the fire they gather around. The headline: your whole Desktop workspace now opens in a browser tab, served by your own gateway. Underneath it, every conversation lives in one place: a single gateway owns each session, and the CLI, TUI, Desktop, editors, bots and cron all sit down at the same table instead of each running its own agent. From that one hearth, Desktop keeps every machine you run Hermes on connected at once, Group Chats route their own conversations, and the terminal finally draws your images inline and lets you rewind a conversation. Around it: plugins that keep themselves updated, price tags and spend limits on paid MCP tools, pluggable delegation, a plugin catalog that grew from about 600 to over 1,050 entries, a leaner built-in skill set, and a long run of memory and latency work for long-lived gateways. This release rolls up and fully documents the v0.22.1–v0.22.7 patch releases.

- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same schemas

Rolls up 299 commits / 116 merged pull requests since 0.1.18, plus 21
pull requests whose work landed through maintainer commits, from 26
contributors.

The headline is research that outlives the chat that produced it. A finished
analysis can be saved as a versioned research artifact with its evidence
references and data-as-of date, searched later, and revised instead of
overwritten; a follow-up turn or a later session finds the backtests already
run through `list_backtest_runs` and reads their artifacts instead of running
them again; and a research goal's objective can be edited without losing its
evidence. Paper trading adds an opt-in A-share five-minute simulation that
settles a completed session bar by bar on a new order lifecycle, with
JoinQuant's limit-fill rules; saved accounts still settle daily. Gildata
financial queries, report-period stock screening and Shannon portfolio
diagnosis arrive as separate opt-ins for Gildata account holders, Gildata
quotes are used only when named, and the QVeris integration is removed.
Argentina (BYMA shares and CEDEARs) joins as a backtest market, `web_search`
can use Parallel's hosted search, and Codex OAuth lists the models the
signed-in account offers. Both 0.1.18 regressions are fixed: a retried
provider error no longer halts live decisions for the day, and a research
goal's answer that crosses its token budget is delivered. Most of the rest is
correctness: formula corrections to GTJA and Qlib alphas, futures contract
specifications and fees, loader paging and ticker forms, grounding of
document figures and their units, background tasks that belong to the session
that started them and survive a restart, and chat channels that no longer
call a voice transcriber that does not exist. The Web UI gets a new welcome
screen and a warm paper palette in light and dark.

body:
## Behavior changes
- `serve`: the `--http-max-concurrent` default now follows `--cdp-max-connections` (8× it, between 40 and 256). With the default 16 connections it is 128.
- `fetch --dump markdown` now asks the server for markdown (`Accept: text/markdown,...`). A `text/markdown` response is dumped as-is. Not sent with `--dump-selector`, `--wait-selector` or `--wait-script`.
- `Accessibility.getPartialAXTree` now honors `fetchRelatives`, as Chrome does: it returns the node and its relatives, no longer the whole subtree. Use `getFullAXTree` or `getChildAXNodes` for a subtree.
- `DOM.querySelector` with no match now returns `nodeId: 0` instead of an error, as Chrome does.
- Touch event handlers (`ontouchstart`, …) are removed from `document` and elements: Lightpanda doesn't emulate a touch device.
- `navigator.sendBeacon` now checks its arguments. Beacons are still not sent unless `--load-resources beacon` is set.
- The HTTP cache database is deleted and rebuilt when its schema version changes.
- `waitForState` now reports a timeout instead of always answering that the page reached the state.
- MCP over HTTP: a request on a session closed with `DELETE` now gets a 404 instead of starting a new session.
- `fetch()` and `new Request()` with a body on GET or HEAD now throw a `TypeError`.
- Scripts inserted from an isolated world (Playwright `setContent`, `appendChild`) now run in the main world.
- Event listeners now run in their own world's context, so Playwright's `focus()` and `selectOption()` fire React's `onFocus`/`onChange`.

## New Web APIs
- `AudioContext` (WAV only)
- Payment Request API: `PaymentRequest`, `PaymentResponse` and their events, behaving like Chrome with no payment app installed
- `NavigateEvent` on `navigation` (`intercept()` is not implemented)
- `PerformanceNavigationTiming` entry for the document
- `document.execCommand`: `insertText`, `delete`, `forwardDelete`, `selectAll`, `insertLineBreak`, and the `styleWithCSS`, `useCSS`

## What's Changed

* fix(engine): a live component that calls `operator.update()` before any `update_full()` no longer loses what it mounted on its first run. Its existence row was only written at its parent's commit, so the first child's eager existence write filed it as a directory node, and the parent's commit then tombstoned every child mounted so far. Watch-only feeds (Kafka, Iggy, any `LiveMapFeed` with only `watch()`) hit this on a first run against a backlog; later runs were unaffected. Items a first run lost come back when the source delivers them again by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2673
* fix(engine): a memoized function whose tracked state changed while its memo stayed valid had its target states and nested memo entries deleted at commit; they are now kept. A component's memo refresh now writes only to the row it validated, so a concurrent run of the same component can no longer be overwritten under it by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2660

Security patch release: `@claude-flow/cli`, `claude-flow`, `ruflo` **3.71.4**. Upgrade is recommended for everyone who runs the ruflo MCP server.

### Security fixes
- **browser tools** (#4783): `browser_open` accepts only a fixed list of plain Chromium switches. No caller value may add an agent-browser option.
- **memory export / import** (#4783):
  - For MCP callers, `memory_export` and `memory_import` paths must be inside the project. Symlinks, `.git`, executables, and servers started from a home or filesystem root are refused.
  - Import errors no longer quote the file.
  - An explicit `dbPath` must be a SQLite database file, plaintext or encrypted at rest.
  - The `ruflo memory export/import/stats` commands still accept any path the operator gives.
- **record ids** (#4783): `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` are refused as ids. The agent, task, terminal, swarm and neural stores load without a prototype, completing #4671.
- **federation BBS** (#4783): a merged envelope's origin must be the syncing peer or another pinned peer, and it must verify against that origin's key. The sync cursor advances only past verified envelopes.
- **ruvocal** (#4788):
  - With no `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, the ruvocal mcp-bridge refuses a non-loopback Host and foreign browser origins. This is the #4226 guard, now on both bridges.
  - MCP server URLs from requests must be public HTTPS, and the connection is checked against public addresses when it is made. Local addresses stay available for operator-configured `MCP_SERVERS`.
- **learning hooks** (#4791):
  - `.claude-flow/data` files committed to a repository are no longer used as this machine's learned patterns, are not synced into Claude Code memory, and are never rewritten.
  - Surfaced notes are one flat line, labelled as project data.

A complete rebuild of `design-taste-frontend` around professional company websites at the figma.com and x.ai bar. The install name did not change.

- **Installs anywhere:** Node 22+ and Chrome, Edge or Chromium, no API keys. On Windows `install.sh` makes a real link.

**Security release — we recommend all users upgrade.** v1.15.1 closes gaps in how sources are processed and requires content-core 2.2.1, which hardens URL fetching. It also ships the documentation rewrite and a handful of small fixes. Validated with the backend and frontend suites and a hands-on pass over the published 1.15.1 image.

## 🔒 Security

- Source processing now enforces the uploads-directory and URL checks in the background worker itself, so they apply on every path that processes a source, not only when a source is created.
- Requires `content-core` 2.2.1 or later, which refuses link-local and cloud-metadata addresses on every redirect hop when fetching URLs.
- `POST /api/commands/jobs`, the generic "submit any background command" endpoint, is removed. Nothing in Open Notebook used it; every operation has its own endpoint. Job status (`GET /api/commands/jobs/{job_id}`) is unchanged.

Security advisories with the details will be published on this repository.

## 📚 Documentation

Every page under `docs/` was checked against v1.15.0 and rewritten where it described an older or imagined product (#1458, #1459, #1460, #1461): one canonical install path built on the shipped `docker-compose.yml`, a first-run flow that ends in a working chat, a complete environment-variable reference, troubleshooting keyed on the exact error messages the app shows, and development docs rewritten from the code.

## 🐛 Notable fixes

- Timeouts no longer read as connection failures: a model that doesn't answer within `ESPERANTO_LLM_TIMEOUT` now says the provider took too long and how to raise the limit
- Error hints point to screens that exist (Manage → Models, Podcasts → Profiles) (#1457)
- Italian is selectable in the language menu, with dates formatted in Italian (#1457)
- `make start-all` starts SurrealDB again; the legacy `SURREAL_ADDRESS` / `SURREAL_PORT` fallback builds a valid database URL (#1457)
- Docs no longer recommend settings that do nothing (`API_CLIENT_TIMEOUT`, edi

body:
- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same schemas
name: PageIndex 0.5.2 — Lower Cost, Higher Accuracy than Vector RAG

body: **Dify 1.19.0 brings nested workflow tracing to your observability tools.** Follow a workflow into the Workflow Tools it calls, inspect the steps inside each invocation, and keep the LLM context alongside the execution tree. This release further tunes brainstorming's questions. It asks fewer of them, starts by asking why, and when there's a choice to make it gives you options to pick from. It also fixes bootstrap problems on six harnesses, and makes the SDD and executing-plans helper scripts much harder to point at the wrong repository or the wrong task.

### Brainstorming

- **It asks a question only when the answer would change what gets built and nothing already answers it.** Otherwise it states its call as a proposal you can correct. It also stops asking about process: writing things up, where files go, whether to look further, and how to show you something are its own calls, and it tells you what it decided. (#2644)
- **When you haven't said why you want something, that's the first thing it asks.** It asks openly, with no example answers to pick from. (#2644)
- **When there's a choice it can name, it shows you the options with a recommendation.** In one of our test scenarios, where a spec gives Ctrl+K to two features, 7.0.1 found the conflict every time but asked a bare "which one?" in 8 of 8 runs. This release laid out the options and recommended one in 8 of 8. (#2644)

Critical security update covering authentication, Cloud connection approvals,
server isolation and encrypted email delivery. Includes all changes merged into
main since 0.9.8, plus deployment, billing, assistant and dashboard improvements.

### Security

- **Authentication dependencies** — upgrade Better Auth and its plugins/adapters
  to 1.7.15 and the Hono Node adapter to 2.1.3. Address OAuth state, proxy,
  consent, rate-limit and static-path middleware advisories.
- **OAuth and sign-in compatibility** — use the provider's supported APIs for
  resources, signing, PKCE and refresh rotation. Preserve GET/POST authorization
  parameters, silent-request validation, signed login/MFA continuation, OIDC
  callbacks and existing MCP endpoint aliases. Register resources and token
  issuers from trusted instance configuration, while retaining HTTP setup and
  desktop loopback support.
- **Cloud connection approval** — require explicit approval before connecting
  Desktop to a Cloud account. Headless CLI connections require the code shown
  in the terminal, bound to an expiring, single-use request and its PKCE proof.
  Recheck the approving session against live state. Share Better Auth's cookie

### Changes

- **Pay per call with x402.** Set `X402_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY` to a Base wallet holding USDC and each Financial Datasets request pays for itself. Install the extra with `pip install 'aihf[x402]'`. The app asks for an API key or a wallet key the first time it needs data. When both are set, the API key is what gets billed. x402 serves the last 365 days, non-professional use.

- **The scorecard moves the weights.** An `allocation` block multiplies each pod's capital slice and each analyst's blend weight by `clip(1 + slope × t-stat, floor, cap)`. Nothing moves until 20 graded dates or periods. A cut analyst keeps a quarter of its weight, and the cap is 2×. A minute fund rescores once a day. A mandate with no `allocation` block keeps the weights as written. New funds from the app include it.

- **Drawdown halving, plus caps on beta, sector, and vol.** At `halve_drawdown_pct` the book runs at half size until NAV recovers. New funds from the app halve at 10%, under the 20% stop-out. `max_beta`, `max_sector_pct`, and `max_volatility` stay off until you set them. Beta is an OLS fit on about 100 daily returns, shrunk toward 1. A sector over its cap scales the whole book. Volatility is the single-index model, annualized. An existing mandate is unchanged until you set these.

Practise for AI engineering interviews against the course itself. This edition adds an interview bank of 482 questions and 60 measured incident scenarios, a mock interview skill, and code blocks rendered at build time.

[Interviews](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/interviews) · [Scenarios](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/interviews/scenarios) · [Skills](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/skills.html) · [Start learning](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com)

![Browsing the interview bank](https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch/releases/download/v2026.11.1/interview-bank.gif)

## Interview bank

- **482 questions in 23 cards**, from math and classical ML to inference serving, agents, protocols, sandboxes and system design.
- Each question shows the prompt first and folds the answer, so you answer before you read. A short answer, a full answer, follow-ups from L1 to L4, and the wrong answers that interviewers hear.
- Every answer links to the lesson or manual section that teaches it. Every number in an answer comes from a file in the repository.
- **7 role paths** pick the cards for a role, such as inference engineer or applied AI engineer.

## Incident scenarios

- **60 scenarios** built from real runs on the L4 and the GB10 in the SGLang, vLLM and Miles manuals.
- Each one gives the situation and the evidence, step by step: logs, metrics and configs, byte for byte from the run. Then the walkthrough, the resolution, and the wrong turns people take.

## Mock interviews with an agent

The new `interview-prep` skill runs a mock interview in your coding agent.

## CloakBrowser Pro: Stable advances to Chromium 156.0.8078.47.1 (all platforms)

Chromium `156.0.8078.47.1` is now Stable on **Linux** (x64 and ARM64), **Windows** (x64), and **macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel).

With a valid CloakBrowser key, the wrapper automatically selects the Stable build for your platform. No version pin is required.

### What's new

- **The newest Chromium, 156**, on every platform.
- **License connection that finds another way through.** When a license call can't get through, each retry now takes a different route to our servers instead of repeating the same one. This covers launch, heartbeat, and close. Seats are also released more reliably on close.
- **Real window geometry.** The window, the page viewport, and the window position match a real maximized Chrome window for the Windows and macOS personas, in both headed and headless. The viewport is a bit shorter than before, so check scripts that rely on fixed screen coordinates.
- **WebRTC through your SOCKS5 proxy.** With `geoip=True`, WebRTC traffic goes through your SOCKS5 proxy when the proxy supports UDP.
- **Popup blocking and navigation limits stay on**, as in real Chrome, even when an automation tool asks to turn them off.
- **A much more convincing macOS persona** on Linux, and **closer to real Chrome everywhere**: canvas (including inside workers), graphics card names, math, and Windows colors and fonts. On Linux, install the Mac fonts for the macOS persona.
- **New flag `--fingerprint-max-touch-points=<N>`** to report a touch screen, like a Windows touch laptop.
- **On Windows and macOS, this also brings what Linux Stable already had:** the more resilient license connection, request interception that no longer crashes the network process, more Windows fonts, correct Web Audio speed, and Google as the default search engine (`--fingerprint-search-engine=google|bing|duckduckgo|none`).

Your profiles, cookies, and seeds are untouched. Only the browser itself is replaced.

## v0.5.62 - 2026-11-03

- Parallel researcher subagents in `/deepresearch`, `/lit` and `/summarize` no longer fail with `args.tasks[0] contains unsupported fields: output`. The workflow examples in the prompts and docs no longer put an `output` field on each item; each task names its output path instead.
- **Pi 1.5.0.**
  - Security: Pi now ships `undici` 8.12.3 and `minimatch` 11.0.3, so the `undici` advisories on Pi 1.4.0's pinned 8.10.2 copy and the `minimatch` advisory ([GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249)) on its 10.2.6 copy are gone. Feynman's release audit has no exceptions again.
  - Long streamed tool calls and code-heavy answers use much less CPU: arguments are parsed once per delta, and highlighting and rendered Markdown are reused instead of redone on every update.
  - Tool arguments are validated with Pi's new schema library. A single value where a list is expected (for example one paper section) is now wrapped into a list instead of being rejected, and validation errors read `- paper: missing`.
  - Claude sessions no longer fail with `role 'system' must precede an 'assistant' message` after an empty or reasoning-only reply.
  - Failed session writes no longer leave resumed sessions missing earlier history.
  - `pi.exec()` no longer crashes on very large command output or hangs on commands that ignore SIGTERM.
  - GPT-6.1 Terra is available through OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and OpenAI Codex; with only an OpenAI key, Feynman now recommends `openai/gpt-6.1-terra`.

## 新增：支持 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）

女娲现在是一个 DeepSeek Harness 插件，一行命令装进 profile（以 `web` 为例），重新启动 DSH 后生效：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:alchaincyf/nuwa-skill
```

卸载：`dsh plugin --profile web remove huashu-nuwa`。也可以直接 clone 到 `~/.dsh/skills/nuwa-skill/`。

装好后在 DSH 里输入 `/huashu-nuwa`，或直接说「女娲，蒸馏一个……」就能用。

## 行为变化

- 在 DSH 里蒸馏出的人物 Skill 会写进项目的 `.dsh/skills/`，DSH 会自动加载。之前会写到 `.claude/skills/`，DSH 读不到。Claude Code 下行为不变。

## 其他

- DSH 插件页显示女娲图标
- 各语言 README 补充 DSH 安装说明

## 怎么更新

git 克隆安装的：`git -C <安装目录> pull --ff-only`。DSH 插件安装的：先 `remove` 再 `add`。

---

## New: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) support

Install as a DSH plugin: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:alchaincyf/nuwa-skill`, then restart DSH. Remove with `dsh plugin --profile web remove huashu-nuwa`. Person skills distilled inside DSH are now written to the project's `.dsh/skills/` so DSH can load them.
name: v1.1.0：支持 DeepSeek Harness

- **Cheaper** than vector RAG: for both index and query.
- **Faster**: trees are created from layout stats.
- **Unified** SDK: vectorless RAG. **Local** or **cloud**, for index and chat.
- Runs on your **Claude subscription**.

Index, to chat, to agent integration, one client.
Local mode needs no server, no vector DB, no PageIndex API key.

```python
client = PageIndexClient()
client.submit_document("report.pdf")
client.chat("What does the report conclude?")
```

## Highlights

- **Flash engine**: the local default (`mode="standard"` keeps the classic LLM pipeline). Embedded bookmarks are consumed when trustworthy, and tree optimization is on by default — `optimize="merge"` for the deterministic LLM-free pass, `"full"` (default) adds LLM expand, which runs a wave of nodes concurrently instead of one round-trip at a time.
- **One complete surface, local and cloud**: `PageIndexLocalClient(storage_path=...)` is the same client as cloud — submit, tree, page content, chat, and agent tools all present in both modes, so code moves between them unchanged.
- **Cloud documents, your own model**: `api_key` decides where your documents live; a configured chat model decides who answers — and the two combine. `PageIndexClient(api_key="pi-...", chat_model="openai/gpt-5.2")` runs the same in-process document-QA engine over the live cloud tool set. Page content flows through your process to your provider on your credentials; `doc_id` targets at the prompt level; `enable_citations` stays with the managed chat.
- **Agent integration**: the cloud MCP tool contract, in-process — `client.agent_tools()` (plain functions), `as_openai_tools()`, `as_anthropic_tools()`, `as_claude_mcp()`, plus one-call `openai_agent_config()` / `anthropic_runner_config()` / `claude_agent_config()` bundles and `agent_instructions()` for the system prompt. Cloud clients get the live server tool set over the MCP bridge (read-only endpoint by default); local clients get the in-process subset with the same schemas

## English

### Summary

This release adds Arena: enter one prompt and optional reference images, then compare responses from text or image models in parallel test columns. Each column selects its own connection and model, supports individual or batch testing, and reuses existing output, session recovery and backup features.

### Highlights

- **One input, multiple models:** add independent test columns for text or image generation. Run all selected columns together, or test one column individually.
- **Keep comparisons side by side:** desktop columns share the available width, while phones retain two visible columns. Additional columns scroll horizontally, with a visible scrollbar when needed.
- **Familiar controls:** reuse existing input, model selection and result components, including Preview, Source, Copy, reasoning display and fullscreen controls.
- **Recover your tests:** restore inputs, model choices and previous results through existing sessions. Reference and generated images use the shared asset and backup mechanisms.

### Product Updates

#### Desktop

- Add the Arena entry and forward each column's selected connection and model through the existing desktop service bridge.
- Capture the selected model configuration for each request without rewriting shared connection settings when switching test models.

#### Web

- Add an Arena workspace with the prompt, reference images and shared actions in a compact input area.
- Support desktop columns, a two-column phone layout and horizontal scrolling for additional columns, with a direct delete action for each test column.
- Continue requests across workspace navigation so results remain available when returning to Arena.

#### Extension

- Add the shared Arena entry and test columns to the extension interface.
- Reuse existing Preview, Source, Copy, fullscreen and empty-state components.

#### Core/Infra

- Add request-local model selection to keep concurrent columns' model choices and outputs independent.

- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NESTED_SESSION_ID`: set it to `1` on a self-hosted runner to have `claude -p` run inside a session use that session's ID and transcript, as in earlier versions

Safer by default, a stricter reviewer and a new animated README. Paid image generation now needs your explicit OK, the five delivery gates mean exactly what they say, and Blog Studio installs from its own branch so Claude Desktop accepts claude-blog.

Update: `/plugin marketplace update agricidaniel-blog`, then restart Claude Code.

### Security

- Paid image generation is opt-in in code. `scripts/generate_hero.py` uses the paid Gemini route only with the new `--allow-paid` flag and a `GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`; without the flag a set key is ignored, the free rungs run, and the JSON reports `paid_gemini_skipped`. Skills add the flag only after the `blog-image` cost and consent gate. The old `env -u` workaround lived in prose, and `blog-image` and `blog-cluster` unset only `GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY`.
- The repair counter moved out of the draft folder, which `blog-writer` can write to, into the review state directory next to the nonce (`<state dir>/<sha256 of the draft>.iterations.json`). An old `D/.iteration-count` is ignored.
- `generate_hero.py` checks every `hero.*` target and `hero-credit.txt` before any provider runs and stops, without writing, deleting or spending anything, when one is a symlink, a directory or not writable.
- The Blog Studio plugin runs both engine scripts with `python3 -E`, so `PYTHON*` environment variables cannot redirect them while packages installed with `pip --user` still load.
- The OAuth loopback listener in `google_auth.py` gives each connection a timeout, so a silent client cannot hold it past the deadline.

### Fixed

- Make Blog Studio 0.2.0 work with the real engine (#102). The plugin called a status script and a preflight flag that did not exist, so it could never show a passing result. `scripts/blog_studio_status.py` is new (read-only; prints the status JSON the plugin parses, with `--draft`, `--project-root` and `--expected-run`). `scripts/blog_preflight.py` gains `--project-root` and writes an additive `evidence` object
name: Claude Blog v2.3.2: safer by default, a stricter reviewer and an animated README

### Minor Changes

- d99fff8: Add an E2B isolated sandbox provider, `e2b()` from `@ai-hero/sandcastle/sandboxes/e2b`. It needs the optional `e2b` peer dependency and `E2B_API_KEY` (or the `apiKey` option). Use a template that ships your agent's CLI, such as `e2b({ template: "claude" })`.
- 8783573: Add `modal()`, an isolated sandbox provider for [Modal](https://modal.com) sandboxes, at `@ai-hero/sandcastle/sandboxes/modal`. Install `modal` (an optional peer dependency) and set `MODAL_TOKEN_ID` and `MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET`, or pass `tokenId` and `tokenSecret`. By default it builds a `node:24-bookworm` image with Claude Code installed; pass `image` for your own. Sandboxes live for an hour unless `timeoutMs` says otherwise, and `sandboxId` is the Modal sandbox id.
- 775a8df: Add `sprites()`, a Fly.io Sprites isolated sandbox provider, at `@ai-hero/sandcastle/sandboxes/sprites`. It needs `@fly/sprites` (an optional peer dependency, which asks for Node 24 or later) and a token in `SPRITES_TOKEN` (or `SPRITE_TOKEN`, or the `token` option). Each sandbox is a new Sprite with the repo at `/home/sprite/workspace`; `sandboxId` is the Sprite's name. Sprites persist until deleted, so Sandcastle deletes the Sprite on `close()`, when setup fails, and from a background process when the run is interrupted or exits without closing it.

### Patch Changes

- 73ce215: docker() and podman(): the worktree admin directories can no longer be renamed from inside the sandbox.
- 14507d6: Add a Glossary page to the user docs (`docs/guide/glossary.md`, in the Reference group) that defines every term in one place. Guide pages no longer open with definition blocks; instead, each page links the first mention of a term to its glossary entry.

## Source-only release

Skill Recorder 0.8.0 is published from commit [`505c97ae47be5642c0e1b44ebb8d1c1530c298fa`](https://github.com/microsoft/skill-recorder/commit/505c97ae47be5642c0e1b44ebb8d1c1530c298fa).

This release is **source-only**. No installers or portable binaries are attached. GitHub's generated archives contain the tagged repository source only.

## Changes

- **Import an existing recording:** use the smaller folder button beside Record to select a local MP4 or WebM, such as a downloaded Teams demonstration.
- Check actual video and audio decoding before proceeding. Unsupported codecs and invalid media are rejected with an explanation; no converter, standalone FFmpeg installation, or new application dependency is required.
- Add optional details to explain the task, supplement the demonstration, or suggest where it appears. Leaving details empty is supported. Timestamps guide the AI; they do not trim the recording.
- Transcribe audio locally with the existing Whisper model, then reconstruct activities from the video, speech, and user details. Silent videos and videos without audio are supported; transcription failures stop analysis so they can be retried.
- Reuse the existing activity-review and skill-building flow: edit, reorder, add or remove activities, then create, review, and install/export a skill.
- Preserve live screen recording, its settings, and its event-first analysis behavior.
- Keep the original recording untouched. Store a local session copy with cancellation, retry, and privacy protection for outgoing frames and text.

## Compatibility and limitations

- Import limits: **512 MiB**, **15 minutes**, and up to **3840 x 2160 pixels** (or an equivalent pixel count). Audio must be mono or stereo at no more than 48 kHz. One video track and at most one audio track are supported.

## New Features

### Sparsity

- Add skip-softmax calibration through vLLM for FlashAttention and FlashInfer, requiring `--validation_prompts_file` and validating serving sparsity on calibration and held-out prompts before exporting prefill/decode fits and their validation scope as `sparse_attention_config`. Calibration uses single-sequence, unchunked eager execution; serving preserves the calibrated 128-token KV-tile granularity and 128-row prefill Q tiles, autotunes only its execution schedule, and uses a smaller Q tile for one-token decode.
- Sparse-only vLLM installs now reject unsupported DCP, DBO/ubatching, speculative decoding, and FULL mixed-batch CUDA graphs; calibrated decode also rejects FULL decode graphs.

### Quantization

- Add metadata-only export specifications and non-mutating per-weight quantizer-state capture.
- Add functional quantized-weight packing, topology-aligned state merge/select and transport APIs, and canonical Hugging Face quantization-config construction.
- HF export records canonical activation schemes, group/block sizes and weight-only MXFP4 metadata; mixed-format exports retain unquantized-layer exclusions, and non-square FP8 block layouts are rejected.
- Add Q8_0 weight-only quantization with 32-value GGML blocks, packed unified HF and Megatron export, and a built-in `q8_0` PTQ recipe.
- Add Hugging Face PTQ calibration and export support for Nemotron-H MTP modules, preserving calibrated expert input scales.
- Add the `models/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16/ptq/nvfp4-mse` PTQ recipe, the PTQ stage for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL: weight-MSE calibrated NVFP4 routed and shared MoE experts, FP8 attention projections, Mamba `in_proj`/`out_proj` and `lm_head`, and an FP8 KV cache. The latent MoE, router, embeddings and the vision and audio encoders stay in BF16, and the MTP rules apply only to checkpoints that carry an MTP tail. It reproduces the released precision assignment, not the released weights:

## Highlights

- **Native sandboxes.** `bwrap()` (Linux and WSL2) and `seatbelt()` (macOS) run the agent in an OS sandbox with no container and no image. They are now the documented default. `sandcastle init --sandbox bwrap` scaffolds a project that needs no Dockerfile.
- **Resume for more agents.** Copilot, Cursor and OpenCode sessions can now be resumed; OpenCode can also fork.
- **`sandboxId`** on the sandbox handle (the container name on Docker and Podman, the sandbox's name or id on Vercel and Daytona), and **`capDrop`** for Docker and Podman.
- **Security fixes.** The host's `.git` is mounted read-only in bind-mount sandboxes, and host-side git ignores hooks and config that run programs. Sync-out refuses paths that leave the worktree, and `fetch` only uses allowed transports. See the entries below.

## Behaviour changes you may notice

- `git config` without `--global` fails inside a bind-mount sandbox (the repo's git config is read-only there).
- Host-side merges no longer run the repo's git hooks.
- Sync-out now fails with `SyncOutPathError` where it used to skip a file.

---

### Minor Changes

- 0210ba0: Add session resume to the `copilot()` agent. Sandcastle now captures each Copilot session's `events.jsonl` to `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/` on the host, and `r.resume()` (or `resumeSession`) copies it back into the sandbox and runs `copilot --resume=<id>`. Opt out with `copilot(model, { captureSessions: false })`. The Copilot CLI has no fork, so `r.fork()` throws a `ForkNotSupportedError` naming `copilot` before any sandbox starts.

The second 4.2 alpha carries every fix from 4.1.5 plus the ones that only land on 4.2: Skills discovery through proxies pages its backends with a bound, pre-4.2 Prefab backend addresses rebind through 4.2 proxies, large tool catalogs expand their schemas faster, and kept-alive stdio transports respect each client's timeout. Before tagging, this build ran against pydantic-ai, langchain, agno, Microsoft Agent Framework, and the OpenAI Agents SDK. Skills support remains experimental; this prerelease is intended for integration testing.

Behavior changes since a1: JSON Schema `const` and `enum` compare by JSON equality, so `true` no longer passes for `1`; `prompts/get` with a missing argument returns invalid params (`-32602`); OpenAPI upstream errors are cut to 1 KB with HTML bodies dropped, and strict input validation rejects undeclared OpenAPI arguments; a later client with a different timeout restarts an idle kept-alive stdio subprocess, while one nested inside a live client shares its session's timeout and logs a warning.

Thanks to our 22 contributors, including 13 first-time contributors.

body:
## What's Changed

### Connector key fixes: no more collisions or lost writes

Every source item and target state has a key. CocoIndex uses the key to match an object with its previous run, and to decide what to create, update or delete. Prompted by the Google Drive fix in #2485, this release audits how every Python connector builds its keys. It fixes each case where the connector gave two different objects one key, or where a key that changed for the same object made CocoIndex delete that object. Two keys you choose can also reach one object, such as overlapping directories or two `ContextKey`s for one database. CocoIndex can't detect that, so it stays your responsibility; the docs now point out where it can happen.

**Two different objects shared one key**, so one overwrote or deleted the other:
* Google Drive: files with the same name, even in one folder. Items are now keyed by file ID by @Sujit-1509 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2485
* S3, Azure Blob and OCI: object keys that differ only in a doubled or leading `/`, a `./` segment, or `\` versus `/`; and, with `prefix="docs"`, `docs/a.md` and `docsa.md`. Paths in different buckets also compared equal by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2601
* Kafka: the same message key on two topics of one `topic_as_map` feed. A tombstone on one topic deleted the other topic's outputs by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2597
* Neo4j and FalkorDB: a node label and a relationship type with the same name, and derived edge ids of different endpoints (`1` vs `"1"`, ids containing `_`). The fix comes as new node and relationship target APIs (see "When you upgrade") by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2612
* SurrealDB: derived relation IDs of different endpoints, e.g. `doc:'chunk_1'` and `doc_chunk:1` linked to the same tag by @georgeh0 in https://github.com/cocoindex-io/cocoindex/pull/2599
* zvec: `1` and `"1"` in an `Any`, `object` o

body:
### Changes

- **Square-root market impact.** Every fill pays impact on top of the half-spread and the commission: Y × daily volatility × sqrt(order / 20-day average volume). Y defaults to 1.0. Volatility is the sample sigma of daily log returns over those same bars. A name with no history, or fewer than three bars, pays no impact. A minute fund's order is measured against a whole day's volume. The orders table splits the cost into spread, impact, and commission, and shows the order as a percent of ADV.

- **No-trade band.** An add smaller than `min_trade_pct` of equity waits and is retried next cycle. The default is 0.5%. A trim, a close, or a flip always goes through.

Both are defaults, so an existing mandate picks them up on upgrade. Set `impact_coefficient: 0` and `min_trade_pct: 0` to get the previous behavior back.

- **👥 Separate sessions in one browser** — work with multiple accounts without sharing their cookies or storage. `browser_tabs` with `action: "new"` now accepts `isolatedContext: "<name>"`: tabs with the same name share a context, while different names stay isolated. Omit it or use `"default"` for the default context. Cookie and storage tools operate on the current tab's context. ([microsoft/playwright#43087](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/43087))
- **🙈 Redact runtime values in URLs** ([#1791](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp/issues/1791)) — session and grant values minted at runtime cannot be listed in a secrets file ahead of time. `--redact-url-params=access_token,code` (config `redactUrlParams`, env `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_REDACT_URL_PARAMS`) replaces the named query and fragment parameter values with `<redacted>` in tool responses. Like `secrets`, this is a convenience, not a security feature. The extension also removes its connection token from the connect page URL after reading it. ([microsoft/playwright#43258](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/43258))
- **🔎 Bound find results** ([microsoft/playwright#42077](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/42077)) — common search terms no longer have to fill the response with every match. `browser_find` accepts a positive integer `maxResults`, returns the first matching items with their context, and reports the total match count. Omit it to keep returning all matches; ancestor paths are unchanged. ([microsoft/playwright#42947](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/42947))
- **🌐 Inspect requests across navigations** ([microsoft/playwright-cli#479](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli/issues/479)) — requests from the previous page are no longer lost as soon as a flow navigates. `browser_network_requests` accepts `all: true` to include retained history, keeping up to 200 requests from earlier navigations. Request indexes stay stable across navigations

Agent Skills 0.6.15 stops the security skill's staged-secret check from printing the secret it finds, fixes two simplify-ignore bugs that could corrupt protected code, and makes the constraints skill's security and accessibility gates actually fail CI.

## Security

- **The staged-secret check no longer echoes credentials** (#718, @santhiprakash, reported by @xmxxc in #717). The old `git diff --cached | grep` printed every matching line, so a staged key landed in the terminal and in any agent's transcript. It also read as clean when git failed. The check is now `git diff --cached -i -G'…' --name-only`: it prints only file names, and a git failure exits non-zero by itself. Fixed in all three places it was documented.

## Hooks

- **simplify-ignore restores re-indented placeholders cleanly** (#766, @Quinnod345, #765). If `/code-simplify` un-indented a placeholder or edited its reason, Stop wrote back a broken comment around the block, a syntax error in any `/* */` language. Blocks marked with `-- simplify-ignore-start` (SQL, Lua, Haskell) no longer warn that they were deleted, and a missing lock directory no longer stops Stop before every file is restored.

## Skills

- **Quality gates that fail when they should** (#694, @mavericksea-ai, #693). Semgrep and axe exit 0 even with blocking findings, so the constraints skill's examples could pass CI while breaking the written bar. The skill now ships a small report gate that blocks high and critical findings, and it says to run each enforced command against a deliberate violation before calling it enforced.
- **Contrast thresholds corrected** (#733, @CybotTM): large text is 18pt (24px) or 14pt bold, not 18px.
- One-line gotchas from @CybotTM: compact well before the host's context limit, which varies by host (#739); keep a contradicting caller or guard in the doubt review unit (#754); and an injected exception isn't a crash, and a mocked transaction isn't a rollback (#750).
- git-workflow-and-versioning fires on a pasted d

## What's New in v0.5.1

Three weeks of fixes for the desktop app: the AI works on the page you are viewing, a style button sits next to the selection, PDF export keeps the crop size on Windows, every answer shows its tokens and time, and models can think or not by a switch. It also brings the security updates of Electron 42.

### New Features

- **Style button next to the selection**: a brush button next to the selected shapes opens draw.io's format panel, for changing colors, lines and text by hand. With the chat panel hidden, a sparkle button next to it opens the panel to ask the AI (#1039)
- **Tokens, time and estimated cost under each answer**: hover the numbers for the details, such as how much input was read from the cache (#1016), and an estimated cost priced from models.dev (#762 by @Zhangxiaoyi688)
- **Thinking switch**: models whose API can turn thinking on or off get a switch in the model settings (#911 by @lq-kiren)
- **Named styles**: the model defines a style once and draws with it by name, instead of repeating the same style string on every shape (#969)
- **Models that cannot read images are marked** in the settings, with a warning when an image is attached to one (#1018)
- **MCP server card on the start screen**, with a short video, and a docs button (#990, #991, #1010)

### Improvements

- **The AI reads and draws the page you are viewing** in a multi-page diagram, instead of always the first page (#974)
- **The canvas goes with a message only when the model needs it**: earlier messages stay unchanged, so prompt caching works, and hand edits made between answers are no longer turned back (#1024)
- **Saved prompts fill the message box** instead of sending at once, so they can be changed first (#1036)
- **Pictures in the diagram reach the model as short references** instead of thousands of characters of image data (#1007)
- **Time so far while a model draws without streaming** (#1011)
